fixtures.city_amends_note: A New York city can set a higher or more restrictive construction standard than the Uniform Code only with the approval of the State Fire Prevention and Building Code Council (Executive Law 379, state pack). The Council's page lists the petitions it has approved since May 12, 2020: one, the Village of Saltaire (home fire sprinklers). Buffalo is not on it. Petitions decided before that date are not listed (the page says to ask the local government or file a FOIL request), and Buffalo City Code Chapter 103 could not be opened to look for a plumbing-fixture provision. The state pack's counts stand.

permit.exempt_list_quote: City of Buffalo, "City of Buffalo Charter Building Permits" page, heading "A Building Permit is Not Required for" (excerpts returned by a web search; the page returned 403 to direct requests, so the full list was not read): "Installation of fences which are not part of an enclosure surrounding a swimming pool" [...] "Installation of window awnings supported by an exterior wall of a one- or two-family dwelling" [...] "Installation of partitions or movable cases less than 5'-9" in height; (ix) painting, wallpapering, tiling, carpeting, or other similar finish work" [...] "Repairs, provided that such repairs do not involve: The removal or cutting away of a load bearing wall, partition, or portion thereof, or of any structural beam or load bearing component" [...] "The removal or change of any required means of egress or the rearrangement of parts of a structure in a manner which affects egress". | Buffalo City Code, Chapter 103, Article II, section 103-2.3 is titled "Terms and conditions under which building permits and building permit fees are not required" (title and one sentence seen in search results only): "All work, materials, parts, elements, components, finishes, equipment and/or fixtures, assemblies and systems shall comply with the requirements of the Building Codes of New York State irrespective of the requirement for a building permit." | State minimum standard, 19 NYCRR 1203.3 (read in full on Cornell LII): (a) Building permits. (1) Each authority having jurisdiction shall include in its code enforcement program provisions requiring building permits to be required for work that must conform to either or both of the Codes. Where expressly set forth in their code enforcement program, an authority having jurisdiction may exempt from the requirement for a building permit any one or more of the categories of work listed in section 1203.3 (a)(1)(i) through (viii). An exemption from the requirement to obtain a building permit shall not be deemed an authorization for work to be performed in violation of either or both of the Codes. The following categories of work may be exempted from the requirement for a building permit: [...] (iv) installation of partitions or movable cases less than 5'-9" in height; (v) painting, wallpapering, tiling, carpeting, or other similar finish work; (vi) installation of listed portable electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation, or cooling equipment or appliances; (vii) replacement of any equipment provided the replacement does not alter the equipment's listing or render it inconsistent with the equipment's original specifications; and (viii) repairs, provided that the work does not have an impact on fire and life safety, such as: (a) any part of the structural system; (b) the required means of egress; or (c) the fire protection system or the removal from service of any part of the fire protection system for any period of time.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Buffalo job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the New York rules Buffalo applies.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Buffalo offices, hospitals, university buildings and manufacturing plants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** New York's building rules, which Buffalo applies, set the number of toilets by how many people the building is designed to hold. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Buffalo publishes a list of work that needs no building permit. It includes painting, wallpapering, tiling, carpeting and similar finish work, partitions or movable cases less than 5 feet 9 inches high, and repairs that don't cut into load-bearing parts or change an exit. The list doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask the Buffalo Department of Permit and Inspection Services (716-851-4111) whether your replacement needs a permit. Work that needs no permit must still meet the building rules. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the Buffalo Department of Permit and Inspection Services
page.stalls_intro: Buffalo applies New York's rules, which count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and any fraction rounds up. Every toilet needs its own stall with a door. Urinals are optional: in each men's room they can replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a privacy screen.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building. An office for 25 people or fewer, or any space for 15 or fewer, doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. A restaurant's count includes seasonal outdoor seating.
page.install_rule: Contractors running a construction business in Buffalo need a City of Buffalo contractor license. New York State does not license commercial installers, though some local governments, Buffalo among them, license contractors. Installers should confirm with the city's Office of Licenses that their license covers the job. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor running a construction business in Buffalo needs a City of Buffalo contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on public work, such as school, city, county and state projects, New York law requires at least the prevailing wage for the trade, with no minimum contract size; the state Department of Labor publishes the rates by county each July. For a carpenter on building work in Erie County that is $38.47 an hour plus $30.16 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.75% in Buffalo: 4% state and 4.75% Erie County.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals, universities and arenas:** phenolic or stainless steel where restrooms are cleaned many times a day, HDPE where crowds are hard on stalls.
